idiom_name: array of plain row objects (node-postgres Result.rows / mysql2 rows)
implementation_notes: JavaScript's record set is simply an array of plain objects keyed by column name: node-postgres resolves every query to a pg.Result whose rows property is 'an array' (rowMode: 'array' switches to column-ordered arrays instead), and mysql2 returns [rows, fields] with rows built the same way while fields carries the column metadata. What replaces the classic RecordSet class is Array<object> plus, when needed, the driver's field list; often the set travels with no header at all because the keys are the header. Use it while the projection is dynamic; when the shape is known, mapping into narrowed objects is the same value with a contract attached.
pitfalls: Row objects are shared by reference and mutable: a consumer that edits a row mutates the producer's array - freeze or copy at the boundary.
node-postgres maps int8/numeric to strings by default (precision safety), so row.total + 1 concatenates; convert explicitly or install custom type parsers.
Duplicate column names collapse into a single key (the last wins); alias the columns or request rowMode: 'array'.
